title: New York opens AI lab registration — a 72-hour clock from January
summary: New York starts registering frontier labs under the RAISE Act, with 72-hour incident reporting from January and a federal preemption bill in the wings; Apple's Claris previews Harbor, a Mac app that clusters Macs into a private AI server; and a paper fine-tunes LLMs by deleting fewer than one weight in two thousand. Plus Gemini 4 Carbon's general release, AlphaProof Code verifying Signal, Anthropic's IPO roadshow, and a Notion vendor breach.

rundown: New York opens RAISE Act registration
topics: New York RAISE Act registration opens (10 November 2026): large frontier developers (>$500M annual revenue, per TechCrunch) register by 1 Jan 2027; 72-hour critical incident reporting vs California SB 53's 15 days; quarterly catastrophic-risk assessments; DIGIT office inside NY DFS; public may file suspected-incident reports; annual public report; penalties up to $1M per violation, $3M repeat; SUNY Binghamton Center for AI Responsibility and Research opened same day ($55M announced January); Trahan-Obernolte Great American AI Act draft (June) would 'federalize' CA/NY/IL frontier laws with 15-day reporting, audits, $1M/day fines; Politico 10 Nov: Trahan crafting narrower preemption

Claris Harbor (leaked 10 November 2026 by Aaron Perris; Claris private preview page): private AI server on Apple silicon, 'endpoint in minutes on a single Mac', no per-token billing, Thunderbolt 5 clustering pooling unified memory (RDMA over TB5 in macOS Tahoe 26.2), sign-up asks company; App Store listing pulled; models, pricing, API format, requirements unknown; compared with LM Studio and Exo

Deletion Tuning (Lu, Yang, Lasby, Pote, Ioannou, Ren; arXiv 2611.10866, 7 Nov 2026): binary mask over SwiGLU gate projections, ~0.03-0.05% of weights zeroed, logits seeded from Wanda; matches/beats full fine-tuning at 8B+ (Llama3-8B GSM8K 83.55 vs 83.24; Qwen2.5-14B 55.43 vs 54.87), loses at 1B (54.44 vs 60.50); 8.4MB adapter vs ~30GB checkpoint; prior-task accuracy within 1 point of base vs FFT -1.3 to -3.1, LoRA up to -5.4; training memory above LoRA; no code linked
